opening.headline: To track who performed what actions when a document is deleted or settings are changed, we examine what administrative controls and audit logs record and what they do not record.
body: Let's assume we discovered that a document from a certain project was deleted and its settings were changed on a Monday morning. A flurry of questions arises: who did it, when, from which device, and on what target? Without enabling logs or knowing where the logs are coming from, we cannot answer these questions.

Conversely, there are cases where logs are present but expectations are misaligned. If it's assumed that audit logs contain conversation details, investigation efforts may be hindered. In this lesson, we will sequentially examine what a manager controls, the structure and limitations of audit logs, and what the Compliance API adds, using the conversation logging procedure as a case study.
opening.objectivesLead: By the end of this lesson, you will be able to:
objectives: Can explain the role of administrative control and audit logs.
It is possible to distinguish what is recorded and what is not recorded in the log.

screens.title: An incident occurred, but we don't know who did what.
screens.lead: First, read the incident scenario discovered on Monday morning. The diagram places the investigator's questions side by side with the scope of questions that the logs can answer.

visual.alt: Four investigator questions, the log entries responding to these questions, and one question not answered by the log, illustrated in a diagram.
labels: What was said in that conversation?

paragraphs: This is a hypothetical scenario. On a Monday morning, a document from a project is found to have been deleted, and it is discovered that certain organizational settings have changed. The security officer and audit team ask: who, when, from which device, and on what target performed this action.

To answer this question, logging must be enabled, we must know who is retrieving it and from where, and it must be retained for the required period. If any one of these three conditions is missing, there is no answer.

Another trap is expectation. It is common to open a log expecting to find conversation content, only to find that the log contains nothing but an identifier. To avoid getting stuck during investigation, it is essential to understand in advance what a log records and what it does not record.

callout.label: Questions to be answered in this class
callout.text: What does the audit log record and what does it not record, and how is it retrieved?

screens.outro: First, let's consider our organization's log management.

screens.title: Recall whether you've actually opened a thank-you log before.
screens.lead: First, think through each question on your own before selecting an answer. The instructor's thoughts will then be organized and presented. No answers are submitted.

items.prompt: Have you actually opened a log file to check it?
items.answer: If you've never opened it before, you only realize the log's format and limitations after thinking about it. Usually, downloading it once and checking the configuration and event types in advance greatly reduces investigation time.

items.prompt: Who knows who can download logs?
items.answer: Export permissions are typically granted to only a few administrators. In the case of Claude, the owners are the Owner and the Primary Owner. It is important to identify the authorized users in advance, especially in case the person is not present.

Varys by service and path. The Claude thanks log export collects data for the most recent 180 days, while activity feeds are retained for six years. Ensure that retention periods are sufficient if you need to track older events.

items.prompt: Do you think the conversation content has been logged?
items.answer: In Claude's audit logs, there is no conversation or project title or content—only unique IDs are stored. The content must be retrieved from a separate path. Understanding this difference is the starting point of investigation design.

screens.outro: These answers vary by service and plan, so I will check them one by one based on the documentation. First, let's look at what the administrator controls.

screens.title: Admin Control: Who determines what
screens.lead: Select each tab to verify the items managed by administrators for each product. The last tab summarizes the common principles.

tabs.label: ChatGPT Enterprise
tabs.body:
Workspace administrators manage members, seat defaults, feature access, GPT governance, apps, analytics, and identity control.

New plugins and apps are typically disabled by default and are enabled only after review by an administrator. Role-based access control (RBAC) separately evaluates installation permissions and app access permissions.

The workspace can display organizational AI policy guidance in a modal and re-display it every 30 days or whenever the policy changes.

tabs.label: Claude
tabs.body:
Enabling audit logs and Compliance API is restricted to owners or primary owners. Audit logs are available only in enterprise organizations.

Enabling Compliance API in an enterprise can only be done by a primary owner, and keys are generated with read scope tailored to the required scope.

tabs.label: Gemini Enterprise
tabs.body: This table outlines security controls by edition, such as data residency (DRZ) and customer-managed encryption keys (CMEK). The available controls vary by edition, so you must verify that the edition you purchased includes the required controls.

tabs.label: common principles
tabs.body: Control is not the default state but the state configured by the administrator. Untouched control is equivalent to no control at all. Moreover, the act of changing control itself should be a part of the audit scope. If it is not possible to determine who made the change, the trust in control is compromised.

screens.outro: Since the administrator knows what is being controlled, let's now examine the structure of the audit logs that record these actions.

screens.title: What is logged and what is not logged in the audit logs
screens.lead: Check which investigation question each column in the Claude thanks log corresponds to in the table. Also make sure to read the content not recorded in the description below the table.

data.caption: Structure and usage of Claude's audit logs in query investigation
rows: Timestamp when the log was recorded
Information about the actor, may not exist
Event-specific additional information, for example, previous name and new name during a name change event
Types of affected entities, UUID, name, metadata
Does this apply to a particular object?
IP address relevant to the event, may not exist
Device ID relevant to the event, may not be present
What kind of device was it?
Header that indicates the program that performed the operation
data.notes: Recorded events include login attempts, username changes, project creation and deletion along with name changes and visibility scope modifications, document additions and deletions, and organization invitations sent and rejected. In contrast, conversation content and project titles and descriptions are not exported and are only recorded with unique IDs. Conversation inputs and outputs can be obtained separately through a dedicated data export by the Primary Owner. Exports are performed by the Owner or Primary Owner via organization settings, gathering the last 180 days of data and sending an email with a 24-hour valid download link. Enterprise organizations using customer-managed encryption keys cannot use this button and instead receive compliance events via the Compliance API.

screens.outro: If exporting alone is insufficient, there is a Compliance API that allows importing via a program. We will examine the call format.

screens.title: Compliance API and Log Retention
screens.lead: The following is an example of calling the Claude Compliance API activity feed along with part of the response. Please verify what information is being returned and what is not, together with the right-side explanation.

notes.note: This is an activity feed call. If you have a key within the `read:compliance_activities` scope, you can call it with any key. If no key exists or the scope does not match, an authentication error will occur. Therefore, you must first define the appropriate scope when creating a key.

The response consists of event records from the `data` array and page information such as `has_more`. Events include the timestamp, the actor's email and IP address, and the event type. Conversations are represented only by identifiers such as `claude_chat_id`, not by their content.

The event type and conversation identifier are provided together, allowing us to determine which conversation was created by whom; however, the content of the conversation is not included in this response. For content access, use the Compliance API path in Claude Enterprise to access conversation and file data.

The scope varies by product. Claude Enterprise accesses activity feeds as well as user, role, group directory, conversations, files, projects, and session content across multiple products. Claude Platform provides only activity feeds such as member and workspace changes and API key generation, without offering prompt or response content. OpenAI Compliance Platform provides immutable, dedicated logs and APIs to query current states, and integrates with eDiscovery, DLP, and SIEM tools.

screens.outro: Having verified the tool, let's move on to the example.

screens.title: Explanation: Dialogue collection procedure and limitations
screens.lead: The instructor breaks down the scenario step by step. Select the right arrow to proceed to the next step.

steps.title: Verify the example
steps.body: The compliance team has requested conversation logs for a specific employee. The organization is using Claude Enterprise, and the Compliance API is enabled. The objective is to submit the employee's conversation records with supporting evidence.

steps.title: Find events in the activity feed
steps.body: First, locate the user's events in the activity feed to verify the conversation ID and timestamp. The logs do not contain content, but they indicate the location of which conversation occurred when.

steps.title: The content is retrieved through another path.
steps.body: The audit log contains only IDs and no conversation content. Therefore, the content is retrieved from the conversation data of the Compliance API or from the data export path of the Primary Owner.

steps.title: Verify permissions and access logs
steps.body: Verifies the range of keys used for access and the owner's privileges, specifically whether the owner is the primary owner or simply an owner. The act of querying content is also recorded. Investigators' access is also part of the audit scope. To ensure audit results are trustworthy, it must be recorded who viewed whose conversations and when.

steps.title: Checks service limits
steps.body: Each service has different access scopes. The Claude Platform does not offer an API to retrieve conversation content, only an activity feed. In the OpenAI environment, documentation indicates that locked conversations are accessible, while in the Compliance Platform, access is also possible. It is essential to verify the scope in advance. Failing to do so may result in being unable to submit materials by the deadline.

steps.title: Manages the collected data
steps.body: The collected data is stored with a defined purpose and retention period and is disposed of once the purpose is completed. Conversation data gathered for audit purposes is sensitive data in itself.

screens.outro: Next, we will see what happens when logging is not configured.

screens.title: Explanation: What is being logged if logging is not configured?
screens.lead: When you select an item to expand, you'll see the differences in logging settings before and after, as well as common blanks. Please read through and consider whether your organization has any such blanks.

items.title: Differences before and after configuration
items.body: Before configuration, export is impossible due to plan restrictions, and the source of the data is unknown, so evidence is unavailable at the required time. After configuration, it is clearly defined who can export, where it is stored, and how long it is retained. Logs are equivalent to non-existent if configuration is not performed.

items.title: Gap 1: Environment lacking a conversation content access pathway
items.body: The Claude Platform organization can only receive activity feeds via the Compliance API and does not receive conversation content. If content is required, the application must separately maintain its own logs.

items.title: Gap 2: Short retention period
items.body: If the log retention period is short, you will not be able to track older events. Audit logs are exported for the most recent 180 days, while activity feeds retain data for up to six years, depending on the path. Verify that the retention period matches the required investigation period.

items.title: Space 3: Area to be configured by the customer
items.body: In a shared responsibility model, customers are responsible for configuring and maintaining logs in their own settings section. The provider's possession of infrastructure logs does not automatically capture events that occur within the customer's configuration settings.

items.title: 4: Constraints of the Export Method
items.body: Enterprise organizations using customer management encryption keys cannot use the export button and must receive compliance events via the Compliance API. Security settings may change log access methods, so verify these settings before making any changes.

screens.outro: Now I will summarize the previous content into a single reference point.

screens.title: Summary: Logs do not exist if not configured
screens.lead: Summarize the content discussed so far. Please read the following paragraphs in sequence.

paragraphs: Admin control is the state configured by the administrator, not the default value. Unenabled controls and logs behave as if they do not exist, and any changes to the settings must be recorded.

Thank you logs record who, when, what, and where actions were performed, but do not record the actual conversation content. The content is retrieved through separate paths such as the Compliance API or data export, and the scope varies by product.

To prepare for an investigation, you should beforehand define the retention period and viewing permissions. Before proceeding, consider who can export the data, how long it will be retained, and where the content originates from. Simply downloading and opening the data once can help you understand the data structure, event types, and authorized users. Remember that the scope varies by product—data accessible from Claude Enterprise, Claude Platform, or OpenAI environments differ.

glossary.def: Settings that define items such as functions, permissions, apps, and retention at the workspace or organization level.
This is a list of events recording who performed what action at what time. It only retains identifiers and does not include conversation content.
This is a management API that retrieves activity feeds and, depending on the product, conversation data programmatically.
This policy specifies for how long and where logs are retained, varying by path.

misconceptions.myth: The conversation content is present in the log.
misconceptions.fact: Claude's audit logs contain only unique IDs, without any information about the conversation or project titles or contents. The actual content must be retrieved via data export or the Compliance API.
The access path varies depending on plan, permissions, and whether encryption keys are used, and some require configuration to obtain. Direct verification of the settings is necessary.

misconceptions.myth: The Compliance API enables conversation across all products.
misconceptions.fact: The Claude Platform provides only activity feeds and does not provide prompts or response content. The scope varies by product.

closing.lead: Summarizes the key points of this class.
points: Logs do not exist unless they are configured.
Thank you logs record actions without recording conversation content.
The Compliance API and data export complement content collection, and the scope varies by product.
Set retention periods and access permissions before considering the implications.

checks.explain: Audit logs record who, when, what, where — including time, actor, event, target ID, IP, and device. They do not contain conversation titles or content, only unique IDs.

wrong.0: The content is not present in the audit log and only the ID exists; the content must be retrieved from a separate path.
wrong.2: Input and output correspond to separate paths, such as a primary owner's distinct data export.
wrong.3: Export accumulates the most recent 180 days' data.
